{{Short description|Algebraic structure}}
{{Dark mode invert|[[Image:Tamari lattice.svg|thumb|250px|Tamari lattice of order 4]]}}
In mathematics, the '''Tamari lattice''' is an algebraic structure that concisely represents some of the important logical and geometric properties of [[associativity]].  More formally, the Tamari lattice of order ''n'', introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Dov Tamari (mathematician)|first=Dov |last=Tamari|year=1951}} and sometimes notated T<sub>n</sub> or Y<sub>n</sub>, is a [[partially ordered set]] in which the elements consist of all ways of bracketing a sequence of ''n+1'' letters using ''n'' pairs of parentheses, with the ordering induced by only rightward applications of the associative law  ((''xy'')''z'')&nbsp;→&nbsp;(''x''(''yz'')).  For instance, T<sub>3</sub> contains five elements (((''ab'')''c'')''d''), ((''ab'')(''cd'')), ((''a''(''bc''))''d''), (''a''((''bc'')''d'')), and (''a''(''b''(''cd''))), with (((''ab'')''c'')''d'') < ((''ab'')(''cd'')) < (''a''(''b''(''cd''))) and (((''ab'')''c'')''d'') < ((''a''(''bc''))''d'') < (''a''((''bc'')''d'')) < (''a''(''b''(''cd''))).  (The outermost pair of parentheses is redundant and often omitted when naming the elements of T<sub>n</sub>, as in the depiction of T<sub>4</sub> shown in the figure.)

The number of elements in the Tamari lattice of order ''n'' is the ''n''th [[Catalan number]] C<sub>''n''</sub>.  Its [[Hasse diagram]] is [[Graph isomorphism|isomorphic]] to the [[skeleton (topology)|skeleton]] of the [[associahedron]] of dimension ''n-1''. 

The [[Lattice (order)|lattice property]] for the order (i.e., that any two bracketings have a [[join and meet]]) was stated without proof by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Dov Tamari (mathematician)|first=Dov |last=Tamari|year=1951}} in his thesis.<ref name="Müller-Hoissen and Walther 2012"></ref>
The property is non-trivial, and was established rigorously by Tamari together with his student [[Haya Freedman]] {{harv|Friedman|Tamari|1967}}. A simpler proof appeared later with Tamari's student Samuel Huang {{harv|Huang|Tamari|1972}}.

The Tamari lattice can be described in several other equivalent ways:
*It is the [[Partially ordered set|poset]] of [[binary tree]]s with ''n'' nodes and ''n''+1 leaves, ordered by [[tree rotation]] operations.
*It is the poset of [[Triangulation (geometry)|triangulations]] of a convex ''n''-gon, ordered by flip operations that substitute one diagonal of the polygon for another.
*It is the poset of sequences of ''n'' integers ''a''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''a''<sub>''n''</sub>, ordered coordinatewise,  such that ''i''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''a''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''n''  and if ''i''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''j''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''a''<sub>''i''</sub> then ''a''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''a''<sub>''i''</sub> {{harv|Huang|Tamari|1972}}.
*It is the poset of [[tree (graph theory)|ordered forests]], in which one forest is earlier than another in the partial order if, for every ''j'', the ''j''th node in a [[Depth-first search#Vertex orderings|preorder]] traversal of the first forest has at least as many descendants as the ''j''th node in a preorder traversal of the second forest {{harv|Knuth|2005}}.

==Notation and indexing==

The notation Y<sub>n</sub> is sometimes used for the Tamari lattice of order ''n'' {{harv|Chapoton|2005}}, which has the mnemonic value that the elements of the lattice may be considered as binary trees with ''n'' Y-shaped binary nodes.  Note that the corresponding [[associahedron]] of dimension ''n''-1 is notated K<sub>''n''+1</sub> since the indexing is by the number of leaves in the binary trees that form its vertices, rather than by the number of nodes.
